route: 9 (response-frequency matching against the source of record) + 2 (structural signature: distinct mark distributions and a matching unused-mark cell)
evidence: imo-official.org publishes both the numbered 2015 problem paper (which prints 'Problem 1'..'Problem 6' outright) and the per-contestant marks for the same competition under headings P1-P6 (results/individual/year/2015/, embedded JSON "scores":[P1..P6], scraped 2026-09-07, 577 contestants). All 48 cells of the item x mark(0-7) count matrix match the live table exactly: problem1 93/89/5/21/72/12/20/265 vs P1 93/89/5/21/72/12/20/265; problem2 256/151/77/27/8/13/14/31; problem3 408/122/12/1/3/0/1/30; problem4 91/36/61/18/11/1/8/351; problem5 153/255/34/90/8/4/3/30; problem6 521/11/15/6/3/3/7/11 -- 0 of 48 cells disagree, and per-item means 4.307/1.359/0.653/4.794/1.513/0.355 match to 3dp on both sides. All 15 pairs of problems have distinct mark distributions, so the assignment is unique rather than merely consistent: every item is distinguished from every other. An independent structural fingerprint agrees: exactly one cell is empty in the official table and in the live table and it is the same cell (P3 has zero marks of 5), which is why problem3 shows 7 observed resp levels while the other five show all 8. Live 577 unique ids x 6 problems matches the 577 contestants at the 56th IMO (Chiang Mai, July 4-16 2015, 104 countries), ruling out the neighbouring 2014 (560) and 2016 (602) administrations. The code derivation adds an independent tie: data/imos_2018.r pivots imo_results.csv's own Problem1..Problem6 column names into `item`, so the code IS the source column name. NOT established by this route: it ties each item code to an official score COLUMN, not directly to a STATEMENT; the column-to-statement tie rests on the official paper's own printed 'Problem K' headings for the same competition, a documentary fact no script can test. It also says nothing about option_text (blank by design -- a jury mark has no anchors) or about the English-vs-administered-language caveat. Re-runnable as verify_imos_2015.R (VERDICT: PASS).
